'''Richard Michael Wilson''' (23 November 1945) is a mathematician and a [[professor emeritus]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=home/> Wilson and his PhD supervisor [[Dijen K. Ray-Chaudhuri]], solved [[Kirkman's schoolgirl problem]] in 1968.<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Ray-Chaudhuri | first1 = D. K.
 | last2 = Wilson | first2 = Richard M.
 | editor-first = Theodore S. | editor-last = Motzkin
 | contribution = Solution of Kirkman's schoolgirl problem
 | mr = 314644
 | pages = 187–203
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society | location = Providence, Rhode Island
 | series = Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics
 | title = Combinatorics (University of California, Los Angeles, Calif., March 21–22, 1968)
 | volume = XIX
 | year = 1971
 | zbl = 0248.05009}} See reviews by Jane Di Paola (MR) and C. C. Yalavigi (Zbl).</ref> Wilson is known for his work in [[combinatorial mathematics]], as well as on historical [[flute]]s.

==Education==
Wilson was educated at [[Indiana University]] where he was awarded a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1966.<ref name=home>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.caltech.edu/people/wilson.html|title=Richard M. Wilson|first=cherie|last=galvez|website=www.math.caltech.edu}}</ref> followed by a [[Master of Science]] degree from [[Ohio State University]] in 1968. His [[PhD]], also from [[Ohio State University]] was awarded in 1969 for research supervised by [[Dijen K. Ray-Chaudhuri]].<ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy|id=10076|name=Richard Michael Wilson}}</ref>

==Career and research==
His breakthrough in [[Combinatorics#pairwise balanced designs|pairwise balanced designs]], and [[Graeco-Latin square#Mutually orthogonal Latin squares|orthogonal Latin squares]] built upon the groundwork set before him, by [[R. C. Bose]], [[E. T. Parker]], [[S. S. Shrikhande]], and [[Haim Hanani]] are widely referenced in [[Combinatorial design|combinatorial design theory]] and [[Combinatorics#Coding theory|coding theory]].<ref name=wilson>{{cite journal|title=Preface: Richard M. Wilson, Special issue honoring his 65th birthday|author=Arasu, KT |author2= Liu, X. |author3= McGuire, G.|journal=Designs, Codes and Cryptography|pages=1–2|year=2012}}</ref>

==Musical career==
Wilson is also one of the world's top experts on historical flutes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Saenger |first1=Katherine |title=Rick Wilson And The "Old Flutes" Website |url=https://www.nyfluteclub.org/uploads/newsletters/2006-2007/07MAY_FINAL-low.pdf |website=NYCF Newsletter |publisher=New York Flute Club |access-date=12 April 2022}}</ref>
